Log delivery/ingestion is asynchronous and may arrive out of endpoint-attempt order. No exact latency, dwell-time formula, stream-shard algorithm, logging retry durability or all-failures delivery guarantee is inferred from this short run.

HTTP providerResponse is the observed reason phrase, not the custom receiver response body. Native 400 and 302 feedback status SUCCESS means SNS completed delivery, not application acceptance. Retries 429/503 produce individual failure feedback; attempts is absent on initial attempts and 1 on the one configured retry.

HTTP confirmations generate feedback, including the two failed confirmation attempts at /confirm503. Confirmation tokens were subsequently used for signed confirmation, so none were intentionally abandoned. Confirmation logs omit messageMD5Sum and redrivePolicy even when the pending subscription config has a redrive policy.

The actual UnsubscribeConfirmation at /200 also generated SUCCESS feedback and omitted messageMD5Sum/redrivePolicy. deliveryId changed across each captured retry while notification.messageId remained stable; initial/retry failure log ingestion order was not attempt order.

Actual dead letters correlate to /429 and /503 notification subscription ARNs and the denied Firehose publication. No confirmation, 400, or 302 dead letter was received in the bounded polls. This is bounded endpoint/DLQ evidence, not a universal absence or durability claim.

Firehose recovery was a fresh publication after restoring the same producer role, independently correlated to native SUCCESS feedback and real S3 bytes. The denied earlier publication instead produced FAILURE with statusCode 400, an AWS-SNS/PutRecordBatch explicit-deny diagnostic, and an actual dead letter; it was not reported as recovered.

The outcome polling subprocess reached its 480-second deadline after retaining the needed delivery and log evidence. Teardown then collected final receipts/logs before removing resources. The cancelled /200 endpoint briefly remained as a Deleted subscription list tombstone; explicit Unsubscribe using its original ARN removed it, and the final account listing contains no owned subscription remnants.

Function URL request events may base64-encode body data; the retained receiver source decodes that flag before identifying notifications. Every retained receipt stores actual returned status, headers and body beside the actual request.

Early shared Python-kernel globals caused the first attempted receiver name to collide with the independent managed capture. Failed CreateFunction ResourceConflictException observations are retained. This slice subsequently used the distinct -http function; the other function and prefix-only resources belong to managed_feedback.json. Broad initial DescribeLogGroups queries may include the sibling topic, while logs projections are restricted to this fixture's two topic ARNs.

An initial S3 download CLI argument rejection is retained. Subsequent successful GetObject calls used explicit bucket/key flags with the positional local output file; delivery body_base64 contains the bytes actually downloaded.

The Firehose documentation describes PutRecord as a minimum, but prior and current actual evidence establish PutRecordBatch for SNS. No claim about per-record Firehose RecordId or final S3 durability is taken from the SNS acknowledgement alone: the retained real S3 objects are independent data-plane evidence.
